title: City of Henderson Aquatic Complex: irradiance sensor fault (2024-02-06 to 2024-02-25)
summary: Irradiance sensor fault detected at City of Henderson Aquatic Complex (Henderson, NV) over 20 day(s), 2024-02-06 to 2024-02-25.
evidence: The site produced 99% of its expected output in the two weeks before, and 112% during this problem (100% = producing what the weather allows).
Output is above what the measured irradiance allows, so the irradiance sensor is most likely reading low (dirty, drifting or misaligned).
recommended_actions: Clean the plane-of-array pyranometer and check its level and tilt alignment
Cross-check its readings against a second on-site sensor or satellite irradiance
Recalibrate or replace the sensor if the offset persists
Treat performance numbers for this window as unreliable until fixed
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: City of Henderson Aquatic Complex: soiling / gradual loss (ongoing)
summary: Soiling / gradual loss detected at City of Henderson Aquatic Complex (Henderson, NV) over 14 day(s), ongoing. Estimated cost so far: $96.
evidence: The site produced 95% of its expected output in the two weeks before, and 91% during this problem (100% = producing what the weather allows).
About 802 kWh lost (8% of what was expected over these days), worth roughly $96 at $0.12/kWh.
The slide seems to have started around 2024-12-14, 4 days before it was big enough to raise an alert.
A slow, steady slide in performance with no sudden step, the signature of dust or pollen build-up (or gradual degradation).
likely_causes: Dust or pollen build-up during a dry spell
recommended_actions: Visually inspect a sample of modules and photograph the soiling
Compare against the decline start date and the last rain or wash
Schedule a wash if the recoverable energy outweighs the cleaning cost; check the rain forecast first
After cleaning, confirm the performance index returns to its baseline
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.
